clue.text: Number one painting

parts.note: 'number one' is slang for oneself, so a painting of number one is a picture an artist makes of their own face

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's picture of themselves is a likeness of 'number one', the slang for oneself.

clue.text: Err by supplying footwear

parts.note: to err is to slip up
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mistake while handing out shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft indoor shoe is a type of footwear.

clue.text: Discover arms initially carried by the French navy

indicators.note: the initial is held inside the other pieces, carried within them

parts.note: le is French for the
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word arms

explanation.surface: Weapons are found aboard French warships.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out a fact is to discover it.

clue.text: Vessel — right one in which to serve stew

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
to pour out drinks is to serve them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diner is told which pot is right for dishing up the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which to' only links the pieces. The answer first meant a meat stew in French, hence 'stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: Its original French sense was a stew of mixed meats, later a medley of anything.

clue.text: Go and marry again

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there
to be paired again in wedlock

explanation.surface: Someone sets off and weds a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: One may repair to the pub, meaning go; read as re-pair it means wed anew.

clue.text: Smuggler on trial — not the first to finish

parts.note: a runner, as in gunrunner, is a smuggler
up means facing charges, as in up before the judge

explanation.surface: A smuggler in the dock comes second in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who finishes second in a contest ends just behind the winner.

clue.text: Standard of perfection confounding most ladies

indicators.note: confounding means throwing into confusion, so the letters are jumbled
most of the word ladies means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: An impossible standard baffles the majority of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' drops the last S of ladies, leaving LADIE, which 'confounding' scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model to aim for is an exemplar of perfection.

clue.text: Engaged in silly behaviour around lake, or the pond

indicators.note: the other pieces go around the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: at means engaged in, as in at work
an antic is a piece of silly behaviour
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: People fool around by a lake or a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pond' is the jokey name for the ocean between Britain and America; 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean between Britain and America is jokingly called the pond.

clue.text: Termly replacement of shrub

indicators.note: replacement means the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A shrub is replaced every school term.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen bush with white flowers, sacred to Venus, is a shrub.

clue.text: Unskilful athlete originally breaks up during training

indicators.note: the athlete's initial breaks into the other pieces, splitting them apart

parts.note: up can mean in, as a batsman who is up is in
PT is physical training

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word athlete

explanation.surface: An athlete fumbles during a training session and splits apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means clumsy or lacking skill, a close synonym of unskilful.

clue.text: Feeble fellow Liberal introduced with biting satire

indicators.note: the fellow and the Liberal are brought into the middle of the word for feeble

parts.note: feeble means puny
a gent is a fellow

explanation.surface: A weak Liberal politician is skewered by sharp satire.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing with sharp, cutting wit is done in a stinging, biting manner.

clue.text: Players may be speechless in this farcical situation

definitions.text: Players may be speechless in this farcical situation

parts.words: Players may be speechless in this farcical situation
parts.note: actors in a silent show perform without words, and the same word is used for any ridiculous, farcical carry-on

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a show where actors may perform in silent gesture and, figuratively, any absurd or farcical situation.

clue.text: Inclined to associate conservationists with arable land

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or tract of arable land
NT is the National Trust, the British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to link the conservation lobby with farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to associate ... with' only joins the pieces; the land comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so having leant is having been tilted or disposed one way.

clue.text: Written evidence producing convictions

definitions.meaning: a written account kept as proof of events
a criminal's list of previous convictions is called their form or their criminal history

explanation.surface: Documents are put forward that lead to guilty verdicts.
explanation.definitionFit: A document is written evidence, and a criminal's previous convictions are their police file.

clue.text: Tune that's appealing to the ear?

definitions.text: Tune that's appealing to the ear?

parts.words: Tune that's appealing to the ear?
parts.note: split as a-pealing: a tune rung out on church bells is a pealing one

explanation.definitionFit: A melody played on a set of tuned bells, or the bells themselves.

clue.text: Shrewd about Italian film's translation

indicators.note: the word for shrewd goes about, surrounding, the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: shrewd means subtle, clever

explanation.surface: A clever handling of an Italian movie's dubbing or captions.
explanation.definitionFit: Words printed along the bottom of the screen translate a foreign film's dialogue.

clue.text: Eat with sailor on ship, producing delay

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to dine is to eat
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Dining with a sailor aboard causes the ship to sail late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' place the pieces: the sailor comes first and the ship last.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness, being slow to arrive, is delay.

clue.text: Scope for raising fine bird — a red grouse

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upward, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: room means scope, as in room to manoeuvre
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Room is found for rearing a game bird such as the red grouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse of British moorland is also called by this name.

clue.text: US president's first changed troops in base

indicators.note: the opening letter of the president's name is swapped for a different letter

parts.note: Harrison was the name of two US presidents, William Henry and Benjamin

explanation.surface: A new American leader alters the soldiers stationed at a base.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new letter: H becomes G, and the crossers confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of soldiers stationed in a fort or town to defend it.

clue.text: Relatively close European

definitions.meaning: in cousin-... the word means closely related, sharing grandparents

explanation.definitionFit: A cousin-german is a first cousin, so closely related; and a person from Germany is European.

clue.text: Muggers grabbing upstart's plant

indicators.note: the muggers seize and hold the other letter inside them

parts.note: a mugger is an Indian crocodile, so muggers are crocs
read as 'up start', the start of the word up is U

explanation.surface: Street thieves seize a young pretender's houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: A mugger is a marsh crocodile of India, not a street robber here.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-flowering bulb with cup-shaped blooms is a garden plant.

clue.text: Conceal correct odds in interview

indicators.note: the odd letters sit in the middle of the word for interview

parts.note: to see someone is to interview them

indicators.note: odds means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of correct

explanation.surface: Someone hides the right betting odds during an interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' takes C, R, E, T from correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something away is to stash it out of sight.

clue.text: State whether it's a mountainous area

parts.note: Mass is a short form of Massachusetts, a US state
if means whether, as in ask if

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to say whether a region is hilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact group of mountains forming a single upland block.

clue.text: Some dire licensee's surviving custom

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dreadful pub landlord keeps up an old tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tradition that persists from an earlier time is a survival from the past.

clue.text: Shy bear, say, or rodent

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: say tells us the bear's name is spoken, giving the sound only

parts.note: Pooh is the bear in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A timid bear, or maybe a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American aquatic animal, also called nutria, is a rodent.

clue.text: Novel is clear — it is based on authentic experience

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book is lucid because it draws on real life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book but signals the anagram; the second 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true to life and drawn from real events is lifelike and authentic.

clue.text: Take steps to thrash with vigour

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to thrash them
go means energy, vigour

explanation.surface: Someone decides to act and beat with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance means stepping to music.

clue.text: Like unassigned work? It could be soon cut

definitions.text: Like unassigned work? It could be soon cut

parts.words: Like unassigned work? It could be soon cut
parts.note: work without a named author is unattributed; shortened to its first four letters, the word for that becomes an old word meaning soon

explanation.walkthrough: Unassigned here means without an author's name; the clipped form, ANON, is also an archaic word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece with no author's name signed to it is unattributed or nameless.

clue.text: Bondsman — one thrown into Irish river

indicators.note: the numeral is tossed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Erne is a river in Ireland
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is hurled into an Irish river.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks the winning numbers for British Premium Bonds, a state savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The number-picking computer behind Premium Bonds is jokingly the man who deals in bonds.

clue.text: Influence a firmly established individual employed to deceive

parts.note: pull is influence, as in having pull
fast means fixed firmly, as in stuck fast
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A powerful, entrenched figure is brought in to mislead people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed to' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to trick someone by a sly ruse.
